title: 3D Printer Waste Nanoparticles and Their Internalization in Human Colorectal Cells (HCT15), as in Vitro Cell Model of Nanoplastics Absorption
content: Rapid globalization and technological advancement have led to increased consumption of plastics due to their versatility, low production costs, and ease of manufacturing [1]. Among these technologies, additive manufacturing (AM) methods such as stereolithography (SLA), and digital light processing (DLP), used in 3D printing (3D-P), have gained popularity. These technologies use UV light to transform liquid photopolymers into solid models, making them useful in various applications, including medical device production [2] and are widely used for domestic purpose [3]. However, the improper handling and storage of 3D printing residues pose significant environmental and health risks [4].
